title: NASA tests pressure sensitive paint on model wing at Langley Research Center
excerpt: Researchers used ultraviolet lights to illuminate a wing model during wind tunnel testing in Virginia.
bodyHtml:
NASA announced on October 2, 2026, that researchers at the Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, conducted the first test of unsteady Pressure Sensitive Paint on a Benchmark Supercritical Wing. The test took place inside the Transonic Dynamics Tunnel.

During the procedure, the paint glowed pink-purple when exposed to ultraviolet lights, allowing high-speed cameras to capture data on air flow pressure. Unsteady pressure sensitive paint is a specialized coating that varies in brightness according to how much pressure the air flow applies to the wing.

This marked the first use of the technique on a large-scale, freely moving model in a low-oxygen environment. The data collected will be used to improve computer modeling for future aircraft designs.

NASA researchers expect to find many more wind tunnel applications for the paint in the future. The milestone also lays the foundation for upcoming tests on flexible aircraft models designed to bend and adapt during flight.
